t: What Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence Is
title: What Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence Is
provenance: JAH Signature design archive: original designs by Justin Addam Higgins. Signature-labeled original work.
description: The Signature Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence is Justin Addam Higgins’s original design. Environments in which people, AI systems, robots, and simulations combine expertise to solve complex problems. This database records the Signature edition: original engineering choices, Signature improvements over the public baseline, and the complete piece-by-piece design. Where public versions of this technology exist, the Signature design is measured against them and every deliberate difference is documented with its reason. Where no public version exists yet, the Signature design stands as the reference implementation. The teaching ladder in this database moves from what the system is, through each piece required to build it, to a verified working design.
key_points: Signature Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence: an original JAH design, Signature-labeled throughout
Every difference from the public baseline is deliberate and documented
Complete piece-by-piece design: nothing required is left undescribed
Designs are measured against public versions where they exist
The ladder ends in a verified, buildable working design
how_it_works: The Signature design delivers this: Environments in which people, AI systems, robots, and simulations combine expertise to solve complex problems. Every Signature improvement targets a measured weakness of the public baseline, and the piece records show exactly where each improvement lives.

t: The Current State of Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence
title: The Current State of Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence
provenance: JAH Signature design archive: original designs by Justin Addam Higgins. Signature-labeled original work.
description: The Signature Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence program starts from the public state of the art and improves it deliberately. Digital twins, automated laboratories, and global research networks are operational today. Fully integrated civilization-scale coordination — discovery through manufacturing in one loop — is the long-horizon goal these pieces are converging toward. The Signature edition does not wait for the field to mature: it designs the end state now, documents the gaps honestly, and builds the pieces that can be built today while roadmapping the rest. Each Signature record marks which parts are buildable now, which parts need research first, and what the public baseline already proves. Nothing is presented as finished before it is verified.
key_points: Signature strategy: design the end state now, build what is buildable, roadmap the rest
Public baseline measured first; every Signature change justified
Buildable-now parts are separated from research-first parts
Verification gates decide what counts as finished
how_it_works: Progress is tracked piece by piece: each component is rated on evidence, from idea through demonstration to deployment, and the system rating is the rating of its weakest critical piece.

description: Four principles govern the Signature design of universal human-machine collaborative intelligence. t: How the Pieces of Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence Fit Together
title: How the Pieces of Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence Fit Together
provenance: JAH Signature design archive: original designs by Justin Addam Higgins. Signature-labeled original work.
description: The Signature universal human-machine collaborative intelligence architecture joins eight pieces — Knowledge Base, Discovery Engine, Design Engine, Simulation Fabric, Manufacturing Network, Verification Grid, Coordination Layer, Long-Term Archive — into one coherent system. The Signature architecture differs from naive composition in three ways: interfaces are co-designed so no piece needs adapters, data and control flow in a single documented pattern instead of piece-to-piece improvisation, and failure handling is systemic — the system degrades gracefully when any one piece faltens rather than collapsing. This record is the integration map: build order, interface contracts, data flow, and the integration test sequence that proves the assembly works.
key_points: Eight pieces, one co-designed system
Interfaces co-designed — no adapters between Signature pieces
Single documented data and control flow pattern
Systemic failure handling: graceful degradation, not collapse
Integration test sequence proves the assembly
how_it_works: Pieces connect through documented interfaces; the integration sequence in this record brings them up one at a time with tests at each step.

t: Build Plan: Making Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence Step by Step
title: Build Plan: Making Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence Step by Step
provenance: JAH Signature design archive: original designs by Justin Addam Higgins. Signature-labeled original work.
description: The Signature build plan sequences the eight pieces into a working universal human-machine collaborative intelligence. Stage 1: Knowledge Base — the verified facts and records everything builds on Stage 2: Discovery Engine — finding new principles from data and experiment Stage 3: Design Engine — turning principles into engineered plans Stage 4: Simulation Fabric — testing designs against physics before building Stage 5: Manufacturing Network — making validated designs real at scale Stage 6: Verification Grid — independent proof that systems do what they claim Stage 7: Coordination Layer — aligning laboratories, factories, and institutions Stage 8: Long-Term Archive — preserving knowledge across generations Build in this order: each stage ends with the verification gate from its piece record, and no stage starts until the previous gate passes. The Signature plan adds two disciplines the public baseline often skips: a full system rehearsal in simulation before any hardware is cut, and a recorded decision log so every trade-off can be revisited with evidence.
key_points: Stage 1: Knowledge Base — the verified facts and records everything builds on
Stage 2: Discovery Engine — finding new principles from data and experiment
Stage 3: Design Engine — turning principles into engineered plans
Stage 4: Simulation Fabric — testing designs against physics before building
Stage 5: Manufacturing Network — making validated designs real at scale

"""Staged program planner model — model for Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence.
Domain: apex technologies and civilizational systems. Deterministic demonstration model (seeded).
"""
import random

class UniversalHumanMachineCollaborativeIntelligenceSim:
    """Plans a multi-stage program: cost, risk, and schedule roll-up."""

    STAGES = ["research", "prototype", "pilot", "scale", "operate"]

    def __init__(self, seed=7):
        self.rng = random.Random(seed)

    def plan(self, budget=100.0):
        stages, remaining, total_risk = [], budget, 1.0
        weights = [0.08, 0.17, 0.25, 0.32, 0.18]
        for name, w in zip(self.STAGES, weights):
            cost = round(budget * w * self.rng.uniform(0.9, 1.1), 1)
            risk = round(self.rng.uniform(0.05, 0.35), 2)
            duration = round(2 + 10 * w * self.rng.uniform(0.8, 1.2), 1)
            # risk retires as stages complete
            total_risk *= (1 - 0.55 * (1 - risk))
            remaining -= cost
            stages.append({"stage": name, "cost": cost, "risk": risk,
                           "months": duration})
        return {"stages": stages, "budget_remaining": round(remaining, 1),
                "residual_risk": round(total_risk, 3),
                "total_months": round(sum(s["months"] for s in stages), 1)}

    def report(self, budget=100.0):
        p = self.plan(budget)
        lines = ["Universal Human-Machine Collaborative Intelligence program plan (budget %.0f):" % budget]
        for s in p["stages"]:
            lines.append("  %-9s cost %6.1f | risk %.2f | %5.1f mo"
                         % (s["stage"], s["cost"], s["risk"], s["months"]))
        lines.append("total months: %.1f | residual risk: %.3f | remaining: %.1f"
                     % (p["total_months"], p["residual_risk"], p["budget_remaining"]))
        return "\n".join(lines)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(UniversalHumanMachineCollaborativeIntelligenceSim(seed=7).report(100.0))
